title: You Don't Beat The Beast — You Survive Her
flavorText: When she steps through the ropes there is no music, no smile, no games. Just destruction. The WOW World Champion plowed through her own roster like a wrecking ball — overpowering, outlasting, outright obliterating anyone who dared stand across from her. Her powerbomb doesn't just end matches. It ends hope. Tonight you are not asked to beat The Beast. You are asked to do what almost nobody has: survive her… if you're lucky.
objective: Survive a match against The Beast without being defeated.
setupInstructions: Set up a standard Last Man Standing match against The Beast. She doesn't talk much — she doesn't need to — so the silence rule is in force: neither wrestler may play taunt cards this match. Pick any wrestler to face her; the challenge is measured in survival, not gold.
conditions: The Beast is your opponent; you may play any wrestler.
Survival is the only victory — being pinned, submitting, or failing the 10-count is defeat. Outlast her.
modifiers: Silence: she doesn't talk, and neither can you — neither wrestler may play taunt cards this match.
It ends hope: the first time The Beast lands her powerbomb, you lose 1 extra [[health]] — there are no wasted motions, only pain.
notes: Slot 1 of Season 2. Teaches that challenges can ask for different things — here, survival instead of victory.

title: Belt Collector — King of the Indies
flavorText: Many wrestlers have laid claim to the moniker of greatest of all time, but only one can crown himself the undisputed king of the indies. Matt Cardona left the world's largest wrestling promotion in 2020 and instantly conquered the indie scene, winning titles wherever he went — at any given moment holding no less than 8 championships at the same time. Now the Deathmatch King has set his eyes on a kingdom of a different kind. The road to a throne of his own starts with one more crown.
objective: Win a match as Matt Cardona.
setupInstructions: Standard setup. Play as Matt Cardona. Every win is an investment — every championship is leverage — so start the collection: this is part one of the Belt Collector arc.
conditions: The belt collector is always working: win the match while keeping at least 1 [[momentum]] unspent — a champion never goes all-in on the first deal.
notes: Slot 2 of Season 2 and part one of three of the Belt Collector arc. Part two goes hardcore, part three goes gauntlet.

title: Raven — What About Me?
flavorText: A former World Champion and a hardcore legend, Raven is a great brawler and a vicious individual — but his greatest strength is the combination of unrivalled genius and charisma. A master manipulator, he uses psychological warfare to guarantee victory before the match even starts, and the flock of followers he cultivated in every promotion would do anything to protect him. He asks the question that gnaws at him: what about me? What about Raven? Answer him in the ring — if the flock lets you.
objective: Defeat Raven despite the Flock's interference saves.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match against Raven. Quote the Raven, nevermore — but expect the flock to have the final word at least twice.
conditions: Raven is your opponent in a No DQ match — weapons are legal and psychological warfare is already underway.
The flock answers their master: twice per match, the moment Raven is about to lose, a Flock member interferes to save him. You must put him away a third time to win.
modifiers: Psychological warfare: Raven starts the match with 2 [[momentum]] — his games began before the bell.
Even flow: whenever Raven lands a successful strike, he gains +1 extra [[momentum]] — the flock feeds on his dominance.
notes: Slot 3 of Season 2 and the first modifier wall: plan around the two interference saves or stall out.

title: Brian Pillman — Loose Cannon
flavorText: An All-American NFL Bengal turned two-time light heavyweight champion, Brian Pillman became something else entirely in the mid-1990s: increasingly erratic, uncontrollable, unpredictable, and capable of anything. His words and actions shocked fans and wrestlers alike — one of the hottest wrestlers of the decade, a member of the Four Horsemen. Now awoken to a second chance, Pillman is on the loose, looking to upheave, looking for trouble, and nobody can even predict what he is going to do next.
objective: Defeat Brian Pillman under randomly rolled modifiers.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match against Pillman. Before the match, roll 2d6 and apply the two random modifiers whose numbers you rolled — nobody, including the game, can predict what the Loose Cannon brings tonight.
conditions: Random-modifier roll: before the match, roll 2d6 and apply BOTH rolled modifiers from the list below. Reroll duplicates.

Roll table — 1: Pillman starts with +2 [[momentum]]; 2: weapons deal +1 [[health]] all match; 3: Pillman may make one free attack after each of your pins attempt fails; 4: your recover actions heal 1 less [[stamina]]; 5: Pillman's first pin attempt each turn is automatic; 6: both wrestlers deal +1 [[health]] on successful strikes.
notes: Slot 4 of Season 2 and the variance debut — the random roll teaches adaptability before streak content ever requires it.

title: Sgt. Slaughter — The Hero
flavorText: Before the betrayal and the boos, there was the hero. Sgt. Slaughter rose to iconic status as one of the most feared villains in the ring — the Cobra Clutch few ever escaped — and then defended his country against The Iron Shaikh, becoming arguably the most popular wrestler in the world. Immortalized in G.I. Joe comics and toy lines to this very day, he is at his peak: a fan favorite, an American hero, a drill sergeant who never lost his grip. Tonight, the crowd is behind him — give them the hero's walk they remember.
objective: Win by submission with the Cobra Clutch as the crowd rallies behind you.
setupInstructions: Set up a Submission match playing as Sgt. Slaughter. Win the way the hero always did — make your opponent tap to the Cobra Clutch. Listen up, maggot: the crowd expects nothing less. And that is an Orrrrderrr!
conditions: Play as Sgt. Slaughter; the only acceptable victory is a submission finish.
Crowd-heat flavor: you start with the crowd fully behind you — narrate each of your comebacks like a hero's rally as the match goes on.
notes: Slot 5 of Season 2 and act 1 of the Slaughter rise-fall-redemption arc: the hero the crowd loves, before act 2 turns them.

title: Belt Collector — Deathmatch King
flavorText: The indie crown led to the hardcore throne. Matt Cardona reinvented himself after leaving the big promotion, winning hardcore championship after hardcore championship until the moniker stuck: the Deathmatch King. But a king's claim must be defended where it was won — in the wire. Across the ring stands Sabu, the Homicidal, Suicidal, Genocidal, Death-Defying Maniac, the man who taped his own bicep back on and kept fighting in a barbwire match. The barbwire is live. Collect accordingly.
objective: Win a Barbwire Exploding Deathmatch as Matt Cardona against Sabu.
setupInstructions: Requires the ATW Extreme expansion for Sabu. Use the Barbwire Exploding Deathmatch setup from the ATW Extreme rule book. The belt collector defends his hardcore credentials in his own signature environment.
conditions: The barbwire is live: board strikes and weapon shots carry their Extreme Edition consequences.
King's gambit: you must win by pinfall or knockout after surviving at least one weapon exchange — no cheap rollouts for the Deathmatch King.
notes: Slot 6 of Season 2 and part two of three of the Belt Collector arc: the hardcore middle chapter.

title: The British Bulldogs — Reform the Team
flavorText: One of the greatest tag teams in history, back together one more time. Davey Boy Smith — pound-for-pound the strongest wrestler of all time — and the Dynamite Kid, whose high-octane blend of technical wrestling, high flying, and smash-mouth brawling changed the sport forever. As the British Bulldogs they captured tag gold around the world; as opponents of the Hart Foundation and members of its extended family they made history. Now, awoken two centuries later, the barking starts again. Can anyone keep up with Dynamite — or stop the man who lifts superheavyweights with ease?
objective: Win a 2-on-2 tag elimination match as the reunited British Bulldogs.
setupInstructions: Set up a 2-on-2 Elimination match with The British Bulldog and Dynamite Kid on your side against any two opponents. The time for barking is over — the Bulldogs are ready to bite.
conditions: Both Bulldogs must be on the same side; both must survive to the final pin — a reunion isn't complete if either man is eliminated first.
notes: Slot 7 of Season 2 and part one of the Bulldogs arc: the tag-format debut, deliberately below the HARD tier.

title: Sgt. Slaughter — The Traitor Turn
flavorText: During the Iraq war, Sgt. Slaughter portrayed an Iraqi sympathizer — and the crowd that once chanted his name turned on him completely. He went from one of the most loved wrestlers of his generation to the most hated, winning a World Title in the process. Colonel Mustafa stands at his side, and the boos rain down like shrapnel. A hero needs the crowd; a champion does not. Win inside the steel with every fan in the building against you — and prove the traitor's path to gold was real.
objective: Win inside the cage while the crowd turns against you.
setupInstructions: Set up a Cage match playing as Sgt. Slaughter, with Colonel Mustafa in his corner. Act 1 gave you the crowd; act 2 takes them away — every comeback now plays to silence and boos.
conditions: Play as Sgt. Slaughter inside the Cage; escape or pin to win.
The crowd has turned: you may not gain [[momentum]] from taunts this match — the boos give nothing back.
Cobra Clutch is your only accepted submission finish; the traitor still wins by his own rules.
modifiers: Hostile territory: the first time your opponent's health falls below half, they gain +2 [[momentum]] — the crowd's energy feeds them instead.
notes: Slot 8 of Season 2 and act 2 of the Slaughter arc: act 1's crowd-heat lesson inverted — win while they turn.

title: The British Bulldog — One Blemish No More
flavorText: Despite his popularity — first-ever European Champion, former Intercontinental Champion, multi-time tag champion, pound-for-pound the strongest wrestler of all time — critics could always point to the one blemish on Davey Boy Smith's record: he never captured a major world title. Awoken over two hundred years after the untimely end to his career, the Bulldog has one more chance to fulfill his destiny. The time for barking is over. The Bulldog is ready to bite — and take his rightful place as the greatest of all time.
objective: Win the All Time Championship as The British Bulldog — erase the one blemish.
setupInstructions: Set up a championship-caliber singles match playing as The British Bulldog against the strongest available opposition. This is the payoff of the Bulldogs arc: the title that always eluded him.
conditions: Play as The British Bulldog in a standard match — no gimmicks, no shortcuts; the title must be won clean.
Run the power game: win without losing more than half your starting [[stamina]] — pound-for-pound strength means never gassing out.
notes: Slot 9 of Season 2 and part two of the Bulldogs arc: the tag arc pays off its own lore.

title: Belt Collector — One Belt to Rule Them All
flavorText: It is difficult to keep track of how many championships Matt Cardona has won — at any given moment, the belt collector held no less than 8 titles at the same time. Every indie belt worth carrying has passed through his hands. Now, having conquered the indies and the deathmatch underground, one prize remains: the one belt he hasn't captured yet. One title to rule them all. A gauntlet stands between the collector and the collection's crown jewel.
objective: Win a gauntlet as Matt Cardona — the 8-title collection distilled into one night.
setupInstructions: Set up a Gauntlet match playing as Matt Cardona. Each gauntlet stage represents one of the belts from the collection — survive the whole night and the final prize is his.
conditions: Play as Matt Cardona through every gauntlet stage; elimination at any stage ends the collection bid.
The collection lores: narrate each stage as the defense of one of the eight championships — momentum carries between stages like gold does.
notes: Slot 10 of Season 2 and the Belt Collector arc finale: the 8-title lore as a meta-objective.

title: Sgt. Slaughter — Redemption
flavorText: The traitor's gold never sat right, and the Sarge knew it. He would later redeem himself, re-establishing himself as a fan favorite and American hero before retiring after a legendary career — hall of fame, G.I. Joe immortality, the whole fold. But redemption is earned in the ring, not remembered from it. Awoken two hundred years later to a world that only values passion and principles, Slaughter likes what he sees. It is time to win the crowd back the only way a drill sergeant knows: a war. And that is an Orrrrderrr!
objective: Win a boot-camp-style war and win the crowd back.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match playing as Sgt. Slaughter. Act 1 gave you the crowd, act 2 took them away — act 3 earns them back through sheer grit in a war with no rules.
conditions: Play as Sgt. Slaughter in a No DQ war — weapons are legal and expected in a boot-camp brawl.
Redemption arc: you may not win by countout or escape — the crowd forgives a man who stands and fights to the finish.
modifiers: Winning them back: each successful strike you land after your health falls below half grants +1 [[momentum]] — the crowd rallies behind a comeback, and the comeback fuels the rally.
notes: Slot 11 of Season 2 and act 3 of the Slaughter arc: the redemption finale inverting act 2's hostile crowd.

title: Mukundi Shumba — The Unbested
flavorText: Legend has it that when The Lion was born by the Zambezi River in 992 AD, he did not cry — he let out a roar that made the ground tremble. Standing 6'6 and 290 pounds of raw power, Shumba is probably the strongest man who has ever lived, and he bested 2,321 opponents during his lifetime without ever suffering defeat. But his kingdom fell, his people were conquered and enslaved, and the man who was never bested was forgotten by history. Now awoken millenniums later, he has a new mission: he will roar again, and this time the entire world will break.
objective: Win a gauntlet without a single loss — the streak that history forgot.
setupInstructions: Set up a Gauntlet match playing as Mukundi Shumba. Each stage is one of the 2,321 — the streak is not a record to chase but a birthright to reclaim.
conditions: Play as Mukundi Shumba through every gauntlet stage — one loss anywhere erases the streak, and the streak is everything.
2,321 opponents were bested without defeat; match that composure — no stage may end by countout or disqualification in your favor, only by your own two hands.
notes: Slot 12 of Season 2, the proving ground: pressure changes shape — not modifiers in one match but compounding stakes across a streak. The vindication: the roar returns, and he and his people are remembered forever.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh — Tablet I: The Tyrant of Uruk
flavorText: Of all the kings that ruled Mesopotamia, the world's oldest civilization, no King can compare to Gilgamesh. Born in the great city of Uruk in roughly 2500 BC, he was gifted with unnatural strength, size, and speed — peerless among his contemporaries, slaying and defeating all who stood before him in the earliest recorded wrestling matches in human history. But this power corrupted him early: he ruled with a ruthless iron fist, paid no heed to justice, and imposed his malicious will on all his subjects. The world's most vilified tyrant has yet to meet the one man who will not yield.
objective: Defeat Enkidu's proxy and win his respect.
setupInstructions: Set up a standard match playing as Gilgamesh against the Ugandan Giant — the animalistic-power stand-in for Enkidu, the wild man sent to challenge the tyrant. Tablet I opens the Epic.
conditions: Play as Gilgamesh; your opponent holds the role of Enkidu — the challenge to the tyrant's rule.
The Epic's first lesson: victory alone means nothing. Win without resorting to taunt-driven momentum — respect is earned in the struggle, not the mockery.
notes: Slot 13 of Season 2, Tablet I of the myth movement. The arc: tyrant -> challenge -> redemption -> quest -> second coming, ending as Ruler of Uruk, Ruler of All Time.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh — Tablet II: The Challenge
flavorText: Then, as legend would have it, Gilgamesh was finally challenged — and this time by a man whose power was truly animalistic. During their wrestling match, Enkidu stood toe-to-toe with the king, not yielding an inch. The whole city held its breath as the two strongest beings alive strained against each other. Though Gilgamesh would eventually suplex his way to victory, Enkidu earned the thing no enemy ever had: his respect. So much so that this friendship would blossom and change everything. Now the toe-to-toe war happens again — against the strongest man who ever lived by another account.
objective: Go toe-to-toe with the second powerhouse and earn the friendship.
setupInstructions: Set up a standard match playing as Gilgamesh against Mukundi Shumba — two undefeated forces meeting for the first time. Win, but the tablet records what matters: the mutual respect born of struggle.
conditions: Play as Gilgamesh against the man who was never bested — the closest thing to Enkidu this world offers.
Toe-to-toe: win by pinfall or submission after your own health has fallen below half — a war of attrition, not a sprint. A walkover earns no friendship.
notes: Slot 14 of Season 2, Tablet II of the myth movement: the match where the tyrant finally met his equal.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh — Tablet III: The Redemption
flavorText: The friendship with Enkidu changed the King. He abandoned his tyrannical ways, began supporting the needy, and used his strength to fight injustice instead of imposing his own will. This redemption story cemented his legacy as a great king and ensured his story passed on through the ages — eventually codified in the oldest recorded literature in history. But a redeemed king must defend his redemption in the eyes of his people, and Uruk watches from behind steel. Fight for justice now — not for domination.
objective: Fight for justice, not domination.
setupInstructions: Set up a Cage match playing as a redeemed Gilgamesh. The walls that once caged his subjects' voices now frame his atonement — win the right way, under the people's eyes.
conditions: Play as Gilgamesh inside the Cage — the redemption must be witnessed, not just recorded.
No tyrant's tools: taunts are forbidden this match. The old king mocked his subjects; the new king answers them with the fight itself.
notes: Slot 15 of Season 2, Tablet III of the myth movement: the friendship's payoff — strength in service of justice.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh — Tablet IV: The Quest
flavorText: Every redemption must be tested, and the Epic tested its king with a quest beyond the city walls — past the edge of the known world, where cedar forests hide things that do not die quietly and the road gives back nothing but exhaustion. The redeemed king walks it anyway. Two hundred years asleep, and the road is still the road: it only cares whether you can keep standing. Survive the quest that forges a legend into a king.
objective: Survive the quest that forges the redeemed king.
setupInstructions: Set up a Last Man Standing match playing as Gilgamesh against your most punishing available opponent. The quest is not about winning beautifully — it is about being the one still standing when the road ends.
conditions: Play as Gilgamesh; the only victory is the 10-count over a broken foe — or being the man still standing when everything else has fallen.
The road gives nothing back: you may not use recover actions this match. The quest's hardship is the point.
notes: Slot 16 of Season 2, Tablet IV of the myth movement: endurance as the crucible of the redeemed king.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh — Tablet V: The Second Coming
flavorText: Now, awoken more than 3,500 years in the future, Gilgamesh — the Redeemed King — is pleasantly surprised: though he died a long time ago, he was immortalized through the legacy he built. What better way to solidify his status and grow that legacy than beating all pretenders to his throne and crowning himself the Champion of All Time? Perhaps it is time for a new Epic. The second coming of Gilgamesh — Ruler of Uruk, Ruler of All Time. The final tablet is written in the ring.
objective: Beat all pretenders to the throne — inscribe the second coming.
setupInstructions: Set up a Gauntlet match playing as Gilgamesh against a procession of legends — the Ugandan Giant, the Unbested Lion, and the American hero among them. Each fall is a line in the new Epic; the last one crowns the king again.
conditions: Play as Gilgamesh through every gauntlet stage — every pretender to the throne must fall to the Redeemed King personally.
Inscribe the tablet: the new Epic is only written if the king is never the man who falls — one loss and the tablet is left unfinished.
notes: Slot 17 of Season 2, Tablet V and the myth movement finale: Ruler of Uruk, Ruler of All Time.

title: The Rise and Fall of Oda Tsurugi — Act I: The Yakuza Years
flavorText: Born in 2361 AD in Osaka as a member of the legendary Oda clan, he grew up a street criminal before joining the Yakuza, rising rapidly through their ranks. By the age of 24, he was already anointed as their next leader. Before the fire, before the redemption, before the fall — there was only the street: no rules, no honor, no second chances. The National Treasure Nick Aldis brings the establishment's discipline to the pit; the anointed heir brings everything the street taught him.
objective: Survive the street years — no rules, no honor.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match playing as Oda Tsurugi against Nick Aldis. Act I of five: this is where it all began, and where the man who would challenge heaven learned that the world only respects force.
conditions: Play as Oda Tsurugi in a No DQ street fight — weapons legal, counting out your opponent dishonors the lesson.
The street's tuition: you may not win by submission this match — the Yakuza years taught pain, not mercy.
notes: Slot 18 of Season 2, Act I of the season finale arc. Five acts close Season 2: Yakuza years -> the fire -> the obsession -> the snap -> the cyborg.

title: The Rise and Fall of Oda Tsurugi — Act II: The Fire
flavorText: But something strange happened a year after his anointing. Oda came across a burning building and rushed into danger, saving 18 souls. Amid the fire, he saw a vision of his ancestors and vowed he would bring honor to them. Leaving his criminal life behind, he began training in jujitsu, earning a black belt and winning several world titles — and the fans took to him, inspired by the redemption story. The street fighter who walked through fire came out a martial artist. Now the hands that once broke the law must make an opponent submit to the art.
objective: Redeem himself through jujitsu — win by submission.
setupInstructions: Set up a Submission match playing as Oda Tsurugi. Act II is the redemption: the jujitsu years, when the vow to his ancestors turned violence into art.
conditions: Play as Oda Tsurugi; the only acceptable victory is a submission — the art demands the tap, not the count.
The ancestor's vow: win without using any weapon-based effects this match — the fire burns the old life away.
notes: Slot 19 of Season 2, Act II of the finale arc: the redemption act between the street and the obsession.

title: The Rise and Fall of Oda Tsurugi — Act III: The Okada Obsession
flavorText: Despite his enormous popularity and incredible success as a 7-time world champion, Oda was not able to establish his legacy as the best wrestler of his generation, let alone of all time. For he was unlucky enough to wrestle during the reign of the Great Okada. For years he worked day and night to outperform his rival, but he was never able to transcend his shadow. Tonight the obsession returns in its purest form: the wrestling machine who excels at everything, who won Olympic gold with a broken neck — the closest thing this era offers to a rival who cannot be escaped.
objective: Outlast the rival champion he can never escape.
setupInstructions: Set up a standard match playing as Oda Tsurugi against Kurt Angle — the Okada proxy, the rival whose shadow swallows legacies. Act III: the years day and night could not overcome.
conditions: Play as Oda Tsurugi against the rival champion in a standard match — pure wrestling, no shortcuts, no weapons; the shadow cannot be escaped by gimmicks.
Transcend the shadow: you must win without losing a single fall — a decisive victory is the only proof the obsession accepts.
notes: Slot 20 of Season 2, Act III of the finale arc: the obsession that broke him begins here.

title: The Rise and Fall of Oda Tsurugi — Act IV: The Snap
flavorText: Years of frustration pushed him to the edge. One night, he snapped: he piledrove Okada on a concrete slab and retired him forever — and thus became the most hated man in wrestling. But it was a little too late for Oda; he just turned 44, and his prime years were behind him. Slowly he was overshadowed by a new generation of young and hungry wrestlers. Tonight, the snap happens again. The slab is waiting. Some men break their rivals; Oda Tsurugi broke the sport's most decorated machine and the crowd's heart with it.
objective: Retire the rival on the concrete slab.
setupInstructions: Set up a Last Man Standing match playing as Oda Tsurugi against Kurt Angle. Act IV: the night everything Oda built burned down by his own hand — the piledriver on the concrete that retired the Great Okada.
conditions: Play as Oda Tsurugi against the rival in Last Man Standing — the 10-count is the concrete slab's verdict.
The concrete slab: weapons deal +1 [[health]] this match — the floor and everything on it is part of the snap.
Retire him forever: you must land a final decisive strike that ends the match — a countout victory does not count as the snap.
notes: Slot 21 of Season 2, Act IV of the finale arc: the most hated night in wrestling, and the point of no return.

title: The Rise and Fall of Oda Tsurugi — Act V: The Cyborg — Banned for Life
flavorText: Determined to fulfill his destiny as the all-time best, Oda sought to reverse his aging and found a mad scientist who promised to make him whole once more. The scientist used banned technology that turned Oda into a genetically modified cyborg with immense strength, speed, and resilience. Now fully enhanced, he spent a year on a rampage, destroying every promotion in the world, until he was finally stopped and banned for life. Brought to the future by the All Time Wrestling Promotion, Oda is ready to prove once and for all that he is the best wrestler of all time. He will destroy anyone who stands in his way, and he will do so with a smile on his face. After all, what is a god to a non-believer?
objective: Rampage through the gauntlet — no disqualifications, no countouts.
setupInstructions: Set up a Gauntlet match playing as cyborg Oda Tsurugi against the gauntlet of legends — the National Treasure and the wrestling machine among them. Act V is the season's climax: the banned technology meets the banned-for-life rampage, and every promotion that ever suspended him gets an answer.
conditions: Play as cyborg Oda Tsurugi through every gauntlet stage — every promotion's champion falls, or the rampage ends.
Banned for life: no disqualifications and no countouts — the rampage is only over when everyone is destroyed or Oda finally falls.
modifiers: Cyborg body: Oda never loses [[stamina]] from suplexes — banned technology does not tire.
What is a god to a non-believer: once per match, when Oda would be defeated, he immediately makes one free attack instead — the god ignores death once.
Immense strength, speed, resilience: Oda gains +1 extra [[momentum]] from every successful strike — the machine learns with every blow.
notes: Slot 22 of Season 2, Act V and the season climax: the only LEGENDARY of the year — banned technology, banned for life.
